review_candidates.title: Director Information & Cyber Security
review_candidates.description: At Bulk, our mission is to build sustainable infrastructure that supports the digital society of tomorrow. As one of the leading providers of sustainable, high-performance data center solutions in the Nordics, we design and operate infrastructure that powers artificial intelligence and the digital society - efficiently, securely, and with 100% renewable energy. We are now looking to hire our Director Information & Cyber Security, to play a central role in protecting the critical infrastructure our customers and the digital society depend on. Bulk builds and runs critical infrastructure, and our customers audit us closely. You will own information and cyber security for the whole company, across IT, the OT that runs our sites, and the software we build. This is a business-facing CISO role: you weigh cyber risk against business opportunity with every part of the business. You will report to the VP Digital & IT, lead the security team and our security partners, and work alongside the leads for physical and personnel security. Bulk is growing fast, and security must keep pace. What you'll do: As our Director Information & Cyber Security , your key responsibilities will be: Business partnership and leadership Work strategically with each business unit, weighing cyber risk against opportunity and finding pragmatic ways to enable the business. Coordinate enterprise-wide security initiatives across units, sites and countries, with controls that teams work with rather than around. Lead and grow the security team, and manage our security partners. Align with the leads for physical and personnel security. Governance and compliance Own the information security management system, its policies and controls, and the cyber risk register. Own compliance with NIS2 and national security legislation in every country we operate in, and keep us audit-ready. Present cyber posture, risk and investment priorities to top leadership and the board. Scope: IT, OT and what Bulk builds IT: identity and access, endpoints, cloud and core business systems. OT: site control systems, segmentation, the OT/IT boundary, and access to industrial equipment. What Bulk builds: security built into our digital platform and solutions, and clear rules for how people and AI agents use company data. Detection and response Run monitoring and detection with specialist partners. Own incident response, test it regularly, and lead real incidents through to closure and notification. Keep our defenses current against criminal and state-sponsored adversaries as the regional threat picture and frontier AI change. Work with national cyber security authorities and forums. Customers and supply chain Represent Bulk on security to international customers: strategically in sales and design reviews, operationally in audits, escalations and incidents. Close the gaps between our framework and what hyperscalers, neoclouds and enterprise customers require. Own cyber risk from suppliers and on-site contractors. Who are you? You are business-oriented and pragmatic: you weigh cyber risk against opportunity, protect what matters, and say no only when it is warranted. You are an experienced people leader who can coordinate across a whole organization. You speak directly and credibly with demanding customers, in strategy discussions and under operational pressure, and you are as comfortable on the site floor as in the boardroom. What you bring: 10+ years in information and cyber security, as a sitting CISO in an industrial organization (energy, process industry, manufacturing, telecoms or data centers) or as the deputy ready to step up. Proven experience leading and developing security teams, and managing external partners. A track record of working strategically with business units, leading enterprise-wide initiatives, and presenting to top leadership and a board. Direct experience with demanding international customers, both strategically and in difficult operational situations. Working knowledge of security across IT, OT and software development. Solid knowledge of critical-infrastructure regulation, ISO/IEC 27001 and 27002, IEC 62443 and SOC 2 Type II, and experience taking a management system through external audit. Experience leading a real security incident from detection to closure. A serious, practical interest in frontier AI as a security question. A degree in engineering, computer science or information security, and excellent English. An advantage: deep OT experience (building management systems, SCADA, remote and vendor access), security in software development, a Scandinavian language, and CISSP, CISM or GICSP. Why join us? Own information and cyber security for the whole company, across IT, OT and the software Bulk builds itself. Build the function and the team behind it as Bulk scales, close enough to the systems and the decisions to shape them. Influence how key operational processes are shaped and developed. Become part of a growing organization with a strong sustainability mission. Work with critical infrastructure that supports the digital society of tomorrow. Collaborate with highly skilled colleagues across disciplines and locations. What we offer our Bulkies: A dynamic, growth-oriented workplace with a strong sustainability focus Comprehensive insurance (health, travel – business & private) and annual health check Additional time off during Easter and Christmas Monthly contribution to home internet costs and sustainable commuting Annual wellness allowance to support an active lifestyle Fully paid parental leave Take the next step in your career and join us as we build the future of digital infrastructure in Norway and beyond! Next steps We review applicants continuously, and we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. To apply, please upload your CV and a cover letter detailing your relevant experience and why you are the ideal candidate for this role. We conduct background checks on all hires. We may also require you to obtain security clearance and a police certificate of conduct. Bulk aim for gender balance and a diverse workforce. We do not discriminate against gender, race, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, pregnancy and/or disability. We appreciate the time you have spent reading this, and if the role aligns with your aspirations, we encourage you to apply! Racing to bring sustainable infrastructure to a global audience! We are a leading Nordic developer of digital infrastructure. Bulk develops data centers and fiber networks that serves as the backbone of our digital society. Bulk Infrastructure is a leading Nordic provider of sustainable digital infrastructure, specializing in data centers, fiber networks, and industrial real estate. Founded with a long-term vision, our founder remains a key owner , ensuring continuity and commitment to our mission. We are also backed by BGO , a global real estate investment management firm known for its expertise and leadership in the industry. Supported by a strong management team, solid ownership and delivered by a dedicated Team Bulk – we build something bigger than ourselves.

review_candidates.title: DIRECTEUR.RICE DE CER et SIERP H/F
review_candidates.description: Le CER (Centre éducatif renforcé) La Plaine des Cafres accueille des mineurs délinquants placés au titre de l'ordonnance du 02 février 1945. Il s'agit de séjours de rupture de cinq à six mois, en internat, avec une prise en charge intensive et encadrée, en alternative à l'incarcération. Missionné par les magistrats du Parquet, le SIE-RP (Service d'investigation éducative de Réparation Pénale) propose aux mineurs auteurs de délits une réponse judiciaire alternative éducative dans le cadre d'une action volontaire et concrète d'aide ou de réparation. Dans le cadre de l'aide à la décision du Juge des Enfants, le Service d'Investigation Educative recherche les éléments de danger susceptibles de porter atteinte à l'enfant, caractérise la nature de ce danger et préconise des solutions adaptées. MISSIONS : Garant de la mise en oeuvre des projets d'établissements et services en assurant : la gestion stratégique et partenariale des établissements. Vous analyserez le fonctionnement des dispositifs mis en oeuvre afin d'en dégager une stratégie. Vous organiserez et animerez les comités de pilotage. Vous serez responsable de la bonne gestion financière des établissements. Vous veillerez à entretenir et développer le réseau de partenaires institutionnels et associatifs nécessaires à la bonne marche des établissements et services. Veiller à la sécurité des jeunes, des professionnels et des locaux. La direction administrative et financière : En lien avec le service financier, vous établirez et suivrez les budgets prévisionnels de fonctionnement et d'investissement et assurez la bonne marche de l'ensemble des obligations comptables, financières et administratives des projets. Vous produirez les bilans financiers et apporterez une vigilance particulière aux questions de trésorerie.En lien avec le service Ressources Humaines vous assurez le déploiement de la politique RH de l'Association au sein des établissements. Veiller à la bonne application et au respect de la législation sociale, des conventions et accords collectifs, de l'ensemble des procédures RH internes. Évaluation, qualité et reporting . Suivre les indicateurs d'activité . Rédiger les rapports destinés aux autorités de contrôle. . Conduire des démarches qualité et des actions d'amélioration continue. Relations institutionnelles et partenariats . Représenter les établissements auprès des magistrats, du parquet, de la direction territoriale, des élus, des partenaires institutionnels. . Négocier et formaliser les partenariats structurants . Assurer le lien stratégique avec les autorités de contrôle et de financement Profil : . Vous disposez de bonnes capacités à convaincre vos interlocuteurs et avez d'excellentes aptitudes relationnelles. . Vous avez une expérience en management d'équipe et vos conceptions en termes d'organisation vous positionnent comme un collaborateur efficace, soucieux d'appartenir à une équipe. Vous maîtrisez les outils informatiques. Pré requis . Titulaire d'un CAFDES ou toute autre titre équivalent en management de niveau 7 . Permis B . Disponibilité pour assurer des astreintes Connaissances / savoirs . Connaissance du public /des activités et modes d'intervention . Connaissance de l'environnement de la Protection de l'Enfance (ASE/PJJ) . Connaissance de la réglementation et des procédures institutionnelles (procédure en cas de maltraitance, d'alertes...) . Maitrise de la gestion/méthodologie de projet Savoir-être . Aisance relationnelle . Sens de l'éthique . Grande disponibilité . Avoir le sens du service associatif et de l'utilité sociale . Avoir une grande aptitude à l'écoute et la concertation et à la négociation

Therefore, our most important assets are the expertise and experience of our team. Highly qualified and skilled professionals, deeply united, working within a framework of professional freedom and integrity, with a strong commitment to progress, professional development, quality of service and innovation. Since IDOM’s foundation in 1957, we have grown steadily to become a multidisciplinary and integrated multinational organization, with more than 5,000 people working in over 145 countries. Are you ready to take the next step? As a member of our TEAM, you will have the opportunity for career development at the highest level in an environment of respect and professional integrity. We are now recruiting Clinical Research Associate I/ Clinical Research Associate II to join our team in France. This is a remote based position with travel to sites for monitoring visits. We are looking for candidates based in Paris or Paris area. About You You are calm, thoughtful, and responsive when things don’t go as planned. You are well-prepared, whether it be for an investigator meeting, site visit or project team update, always staying two steps ahead of the game. review_candidates.title: Chief Operating Officer
review_candidates.description: About the job Lead with purpose. Drive excellence. Make a lasting impact. St John of God Accord (Accord), a leading NFP disability services provider in Victoria, is seeking an exceptional executive leader to join our highly regarded Executive Leadership Team as Chief Operating Officer (COO) . At Accord, we work alongside people with disabilities to support their independence, choice, and wellbeing. Through a broad range of person-centred services, we empower individuals to live fulfilling lives on their own terms. As an inclusive organisation, we proudly support more than 1,000 clients across metropolitan Melbourne with diverse needs, goals, and aspirations. Our Services Our comprehensive range of support services includes: Supported Independent Living (SIL) Short-Term Respite (STR) Support Coordination Group Programs Individualised Support Positive Behaviour Support Psychology Speech Pathology About The Role Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and working as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the COO is responsible for leading operational excellence, service quality, organisational performance, innovation, and growth across Accord's service portfolio. This is a pivotal leadership position requiring an experienced executive who can successfully balance strategic direction with operational delivery while ensuring exceptional outcomes for clients, families, employees, and stakeholders. Key Responsibilities Provide inspiring leadership to operational teams, fostering capability, accountability, and a culture of continuous improvement. Build and sustain high-performing teams through coaching, empowerment, and leadership development. Partner with the CEO and Executive Team to optimise the relationship between service delivery, workforce performance, financial sustainability, and strategic priorities. Drive achievement of growth, innovation, quality, and operational objectives aligned with Accord's strategic plan. Ensure compliance with all legislative, contractual, regulatory, and accreditation requirements while meeting performance and budget targets. Lead quality assurance activities, audits, and reviews to identify opportunities for improvement and implement appropriate corrective actions. Champion the ongoing implementation and enhancement of Accord's Client Engagement Framework. Oversee service delivery performance, productivity, resource utilisation, and operational efficiency to ensure sustainable and cost-effective outcomes. About You You are an accomplished executive with a proven track record of leading complex service organisations and delivering sustainable operational and commercial outcomes. You bring strong strategic capability, excellent people leadership skills, and a genuine commitment to improving the lives of people with disabilities. To be successful in this role, you will possess: Significant executive leadership experience within disability, community services, health, or a related sector. Strong understanding of the NDIS and the evolving disability services landscape. Demonstrated success leading organisational transformation, service growth, and cultural change. Exceptional stakeholder engagement, influencing, and relationship-building skills. Proven ability to develop leaders and build a resilient, high-performing workforce. Sound commercial acumen, strategic planning capability, and risk management expertise. A calm, resilient, and decisive leadership style, particularly during periods of growth and change. Relevant tertiary qualifications, with postgraduate qualifications highly regarded. Most importantly, you are a values-driven and inclusive leader who authentically demonstrates the Vision, Mission, and Values of St John of God Health Care. Through an empowering and servant leadership approach, you inspire others, foster innovation, and create an environment where people and services can thrive. Why Join Accord? We offer a rewarding executive career opportunity within a purpose-driven organisation committed to making a meaningful difference. Benefits include: Highly competitive remuneration package. Permanent full-time position (38 hours per week). Salary packaging of up to $18,550 on a range of living expenses, including mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, and holiday accommodation. Additional salary packaging opportunities, including: Novated leasing Work-related expenses Self-education expenses Additional superannuation contributions A healthy work-life balance through flexible work options, additional purchased leave and well-being programs Employee discounts on St John of God Hospital and Medical Services and Private Health Insurance. How To Apply Please submit: A current resume; and A cover letter of no more than two (2) pages outlining your suitability for the role and addressing the key selection requirements. For general enquiries regarding the recruitment process, please contact Mel Schook, Talent Acquisition Lead, on (08) 6116 0534. For enquiries regarding the role, please contact Silvana Gugliandolo, Acting Chief Executive Officer, on (03) 8468 1102. Applications will be assessed as they are received. Accord reserves the right to commence interviews and close the advertisement prior to the closing date if a suitable candidate is identified. Join us and help create a future where people with disabilities are empowered to live meaningful, independent, and fulfilling lives. St John of God Accord (SJGA) complies with the NDIS Quality & Safeguards Commission, and all prospective employees are required to have a current NDIS Worker Screening Clearance to ensure the safety and wellbeing of people with a disability.

review_candidates.title: Chief Fundraising and Engagement Officer
review_candidates.description: For over three decades, Ronald McDonald House Charities New Zealand (RMHC New Zealand) has provided a ‘home-away-from-home’ for Kiwi families when their child is hospitalised. Through our House and Family Room programmes, we provide free accommodation and practical support, allowing whānau to focus on what matters most: each other. This newly created executive role is a rare opportunity to shape RMHC New Zealand’s revenue strategy, strengthening and diversifying the income and supporter relationships that sustain our mahi. As the needs of the families and communities we serve continue to evolve, this role will help ensure we have the revenue capability and relationships needed to support more whānau across Aotearoa into the future. About the role | Mō te tūranga As Chief Fundraising and Engagement Officer , you will lead an organisation-wide revenue and engagement strategy that supports RMHC New Zealand’s mission, growth ambitions and future direction. Reporting to the CEO and partnering closely with the Executive Leadership Team and leaders across the motu, you will bring together fundraising, partnerships, marketing, communications and supporter engagement to strengthen revenue growth and long-term financial sustainability. With direct accountability for growing and diversifying our funding base, you will deepen supporter relationships, identify new opportunities and build the systems, partnerships and organisational capability required to deliver. This is a strategic executive leadership position in a national organisation undergoing evolution, and success will require a leader who is equally comfortable setting direction, building influential relationships and working hands-on to drive delivery. Key Focus Areas Developing and implementing a clear, long-term revenue and engagement strategy that supports RMHC New Zealand’s mission, growth ambitions and financial sustainability. Growing and diversifying revenue through partnerships, philanthropy, individual giving, community fundraising, events, trusts and grants. Strengthening supporter acquisition, engagement and retention through a clear audience strategy and exceptional supporter experience. Building a connected, high-performing Revenue and Engagement function that aligns fundraising, partnerships, marketing, communications and brand around shared growth priorities. Building and maintaining influential relationships with major donors, partners, funders and key stakeholders, including the strategic partnership with McDonald's New Zealand. Leveraging data, insights and performance measures to inform decision-making, improve effectiveness and drive revenue growth. Leading and developing a high-performing Revenue and Engagement team, while contributing as a trusted member of the Executive Leadership Team and advising the CEO and Board on revenue performance, opportunities and risks. About you | Mōu To succeed in this role, you will be an experienced senior leader who brings strategic leadership, commercial acumen, exceptional relationship-building capability and the ability to translate ambition into sustainable growth. Key Requirements Proven executive or senior leadership experience, with a track record of growing and diversifying revenue. Demonstrated success developing and executing growth strategies across fundraising, partnerships, marketing, audience engagement, commercial growth or related disciplines. Strong strategic, commercial and financial acumen, with the ability to identify opportunities, navigate complexity and translate strategy and engagement into sustained revenue growth. Demonstrated experience building and leading high-performing teams, driving capability uplift and leading through organisational change. Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the credibility to engage effectively with Boards, executive leaders, donors, partners and other senior stakeholders. A collaborative, values-led leadership style and the ability to thrive in a dynamic, evolving environment. Experience in the not-for-profit sector is advantageous but not essential. A practical understanding of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and a genuine commitment to inclusive, culturally responsive leadership will be important in this role. Why this role? | He aha tēnei tūranga? This is a meaningful opportunity for a senior leader with significant revenue growth, fundraising, partnerships or commercial experience who is passionate about making a difference and motivated by purpose, values and practical impact. You will have the opportunity to build something enduring: a stronger, more diverse revenue foundation that enables RMHC New Zealand to be there for whānau when they need us most. How to apply | Me pēhea te tono Applications close at 9.00am Tuesday, 20 October 2026 . For a confidential kōrero or to request a copy of the position description, please contact Moana Temel at Niche Recruitment: E: moana.temel@nicherecruitment.co.nz M: 021 499 902 Applicants must hold the right to work in New Zealand and be currently residing in New Zealand.
